title: Drain the ponds, keep the good ones
hook: Frogs live in 60 of 100 ponds. Drain 70 ponds and 30 good ones remain. Enough?

doesNotKnow: that a species living as many small populations needs empty patches to be refilled faster than occupied ones die out, so it is lost before the last good patch goes

misconception: As long as some good habitat is left, the species that lives there will hang on in it.
objective: The learner can explain that each pond's frogs die out now and then and only frogs from other ponds refill it, so with 70 of 100 ponds drained refills come too slowly and the frogs vanish though 30 good ponds remain.

claims.text: In the lesson's model (seed 1), after 70 of 100 ponds are drained (19 good ponds with frogs left) the frogs are gone by year 23 though 30 good ponds remain; across seeds 1 to 1,000 they are gone by year 100 in 996. Reveal: "With 70 ponds drained, the frogs were gone by year 23, though 30 good ponds were still there." (the year is read from the learner's current run: seed 2 gives 21). Stage: "... 70: gone, year 23" (run log; the first entry reads "30 drained: 33 ponds").
claims.source: runPonds() in Demo.tsx (kit mulberry32, one stream per run, ponds in index order, drained ponds draw nothing). Builder re-run 2026-10-14 (node strip-types on the Demo.tsx function), seeds 1-12, drain 70: extinct in years 23, 21, 14, 19, 23, 24, 35, 21, 16, 29, 33, 60; start 19 frog ponds. Seeds 1-1,000 count (996 extinct by year 100) from check script E3, company/domains/briefs/checks/life-wave-j-check.mjs, same model and draw order (its mulberry32 matches the kit's on seeds 1-12 for all three drains).
claims.note: Re-ran runPonds() copied from Demo.tsx with the kit's mulberry32: drain 70, seed 1, start 19, extinct year 23. Seeds 1-12: 23, 21, 14, 19, 23, 24, 35, 21, 16, 29, 33, 60. Seeds 1-1,000: 996 extinct by year 100. All match the claim and check script E3 (re-run).

claims.text: After 30 ponds are drained, frogs persist (33 ponds at year 100, seed 1; no seed of 1,000 died out by year 100). The 'New seed' button cycles seeds 1 to 12; in all 12, drain 70 dies out by year 100 and drain 30 does not, so the reveal's sentence holds on every reachable seed. Reveal: "Draining 30 left frogs in 33 ponds." (or, if only drain 50 was tried, its own result).
claims.source: runPonds() seeds 1-12, drain 30 at year 100: 33, 8, 6, 26, 18, 26, 16, 28, 19, 12, 20, 29 ponds; drain 50: extinct in 67, 83, -, -, 32, 45, -, 66, -, 45, 43, - (5, 6, 9, 8, 7 ponds left where not). Check script E3: drain 30, seeds 1-1,000, none extinct, mean 25.8. Seed range 1-12 is the builder's choice (the first 12, not filtered), disclosed here.
claims.note: Checked every seed 1-12, as the reveal can quote any seed New seed reaches (it cycles 12 -> 1). Drain 30 at year 100: 33, 8, 6, 26, 18, 26, 16, 28, 19, 12, 20, 29, never extinct. Drain 70: extinct in all 12, so the reveal's 'gone by year {extinctYear ?? 100}' never falls back to 100. Drain 50: extinct in 67, 83, -, -, 32, 45, -, 66, -, 45, 43, - (5, 6, 9, 8, 7 left otherwise). The reveal branch for a 50-only learner ('frogs until year 67' or 'frogs in 5 ponds') is true for each seed. Seeds 1-1,000: drain 30 never extinct, mean 25.84.

claims.text: Ponds lose their frogs now and then, and only other ponds' frogs refill them: with few frog ponds, refills come too slowly. Stage: "Start: 19 frog ponds, refill chance 9% a year" against "empties with chance 20%".
claims.source: Model rule: refill chance 1 - 0.995^n with n occupied ponds: n = 60 -> 26%, 42 -> 19%, 19 -> 9%. With 19 occupied of 30 good ponds, expected losses 0.2 x 19 = 3.8 a year vs gains 0.09 x 11 = 1.0 a year, so the count falls.
claims.note: Reset to unverified by demo-builder (W-839, 2026-10-14): reveal sentence reworded (learner r10); previously verified by fact-checker on 2026-10-14. Earlier note: Model rule read in runPonds (refill 1 - 0.995^n with n counted at the start of the year). refill(): 60 -> 26%, 42 -> 19%, 19 -> 9% (0.0908). 0.2 x 19 = 3.8 losses against 0.0908 x 11 = 1.0 gains.

claims.text: Averaged out (the deterministic, Levins version of this model), frogs vanish once 60% (of ponds) are drained, the share that had them. Short of that, bad luck can still end them: drained 50, half the runs die out within 100 years (496 of 1,000 seeds; the average model settles near 9 frog ponds there).
claims.source: Levins with habitat loss: dp/dt = c p (1 - D - p) - e p; equilibrium p* = 1 - D - e/c. Before loss (D = 0) p* = 1 - e/c = 0.6 (e/c = 0.4 as set by the brief; check E3 prints p* = 0.6, 0.3, 0.1, 0, 0 for D = 0, 0.3, 0.5, 0.6, 0.7). p* = 0 when D = 1 - e/c = 0.6. Optional literature context (Levins 1969; Nee and May 1992, J. Anim. Ecol. 61) is not on the card: unverified, needs a human source check. Note for the fact-checker: e/c = 0.4 is the brief's Levins analogue (die-out 0.2 vs colonisation 0.005 x 100 ponds = 0.5), not fitted to the stochastic grid. Builder node re-run 2026-10-14 (kit mulberry32, this model): mean-field n' = 0.8 n + (H - n)(1 - 0.995^n) settles at 27.3, 9.2, 0.1 and 0.0 frog ponds for drain 30, 50, 60, 70 (threshold H = 40, drain 60%); stochastic seeds 1-1,000 die out by year 100 in 0, 496, 921 and 996 runs; seeds 1-12 at drain 50: 7 die out (years 67, 83, 32, 45, 66, 45, 43), 5 survive with 5-9 ponds.
claims.note: Reset to unverified by demo-builder (W-839, 2026-10-14): learner r10: the 60% line contradicted drain-50 extinctions; now stated as the average-model line, with drain 50's chance extinctions; previously verified by fact-checker on 2026-10-14. Earlier note: Derivation re-done: dp/dt = c p (1 - D - p) - e p gives p* = 1 - D - e/c. With e = 0.2 and c = 0.005 x 100 = 0.5, e/c = 0.4: p*(0) = 0.6, which matches the 60 ponds that start occupied, and p* = 0 at D = 0.6. 'The simplest version' is the deterministic Levins analogue, as the source says. Levins (1969) and Nee and May (1992) are not on the card and were not opened.

claims.text: Locked stage: 100 ponds; 60 have frogs. Question: drain 70 ponds, 30 good ponds are left, 19 with frogs.
claims.source: Ponds 0-59 start occupied; drained = (i x 37) mod 100 < 70 removes 70 ponds, 41 of them occupied, leaving 19 occupied of 30 good (runPonds start = 19).
claims.note: drainedAt(): 37 is coprime with 100, so drains 30/50/70 remove exactly 30/50/70 ponds, of which 18/30/41 were occupied. That leaves 42/30/19 occupied, and 19 of 30 good ponds at drain 70 (node).

recall.question: A butterfly lives in 50 meadows. Half the meadows are ploughed, and 25 good meadows remain. Why can it still vanish?
options: Each meadow's butterflies die out now and then, and with few occupied meadows the empty ones are refilled too slowly
The remaining meadows are too small for any butterflies
It cannot vanish while good meadows remain
recall.why: Local populations wink out by chance and are refilled from neighbours. With too few occupied patches, refills fall behind losses and the species is lost while good habitat is still there.
